mandate.engine_chain: cell -> compile -> jobs -> attempts -> ledger -> measurement -> policy -> compare -> adapt

field_legend.status: published rule status from the frozen mandate: 'instrumented [M]' | 'proposed [C]' | 'decided'
field_legend.evidence_class: provenance of the rule's inputs per the frozen mandate: M measured | C computed | P modeled/policy | X external
field_legend.existing_backend_source: a real file/table/endpoint in THIS repo, or the literal NONE. Declaration in LEDGER_FIELDS without a writer is NOT a source; it is listed in missing_record_fields.
field_legend.surface: the PRIMARY operator surface: rest = visible at rest on the resting screen | drill = requires selecting a run/lens | alert = raised to the operator for triage
field_legend.surfaces: every surface the rule would occupy once implemented
field_legend.missing_record_fields: fields the backend does not emit today (gaps, not assumptions)

workforce_groups.basis: human + AI, per session (frozen mandate: Rules 1-5)

rules.action: Route: default-route to high-Grit models; exclude low-Grit models from unsupervised jobs (J9 / R4a routing).
rules.cost_of_missing: A low-Grit model stays in unsupervised production; correctness silently collapses under degraded input and the operator cannot see which model or operator caused it.

Drill the run's R4c evidence ladder and confirm the model's measured test_executed_success and perturbation_strength. PASS: an at-rest Grit signal exists and each run row carries its model's measured test_executed_success; FAIL: Grit appears only on the website, never in the room.

rules.operator_decision: Whether to commit to a compounding (one-way-door) architecture and how to budget the N-session cost arc before the quadratic growth locks in.
rules.existing_backend_source: scripts/lab_story_arc.py (snowball_factor:139-142, session costs:149-150) reads the canonical corpus (canonical_corpus.load_canonical_tables) and publishes apps/website/data.js labs.story_arc (~:5546); design_parameters.beta (~:3687). beta is a calibrated input, not measured. No Control Room endpoint projects the arc or beta.
missing_record_fields: per-session cost arc in the room
beta provenance (calibrated vs measured) surfaced with the projection
rules.action: Budget: decide the architecture on the projected N^2 curve and reserve the multi-session cost before committing (one-way door).
rules.cost_of_missing: A one-way-door architecture is chosen without seeing the quadratic cost arc; the overrun appears only after the compounding is irreversible.
rules.acceptance_walkthrough: 1. Open L-MONEY or the story-arc drill-down. 2. Confirm session1..sessionN costs and the snowball_factor are shown for a selected story. 3. Confirm beta is labeled calibrated [P]. PASS: the arc trend and its beta provenance are visible before an architecture decision; FAIL: only a single total cost is shown.

rules.action: Budget: pick the energy scenario and hedge horizon; recalibrate EPM for the operator's region.
rules.cost_of_missing: Long-horizon compute inflation is invisible; the model/provider selection is made without the horizon at which local energy flips it.

PASS: the operator can see and switch the EPM scenario with its provenance; FAIL: energy is absent from the room.

rules.operator_decision: Whether to retry, escalate, or abandon a failed attempt: price the accepted outcome, not the prompt, using the attempt ledger's first-pass and independent-evaluator verdicts.
rules.existing_backend_source: attempt_number/accepted/first_pass EMITTED on the workflow-run ledger (experiment_spec.py:362,377-379; runtime/workflow_runner.py:2793-2796); test_executed_success from runtime/test_runner.py. evaluator_independent has NO writer (declared only). apps/website/data.js publishes derived.overall_pass_rate (~:1497) and verdicts.cap_2b verified_success_rate (~:6634). No Control Room endpoint exposes first_pass/accepted; /api/glance shows only attempt.number.
missing_record_fields: first_pass / accepted in the live run sample
room projection of the attempt chain (parent_attempt_id)
rules.action: Triage/decide: on a failed verification, retry or escalate (J2/J3) and set the retry budget by accepted outcome, not by prompt price.
rules.cost_of_missing: A cheaper model keeps a false price advantage because retries, failed verification, and escalation are not priced into the accepted outcome; the operator retries blind.
rules.acceptance_walkthrough: 1. Wait for a verification-failure alert (ON-A1) on R1 (J2). 2. Drill R4a/R4c and confirm attempt_number, first_pass/accepted, and the independent test verdict are shown. 3. Confirm a safe retry/escalate action with remaining budget. PASS: a failed attempt raises with its first_pass/evaluator evidence and a bounded retry action; FAIL: failure is visible only as a status with no attempt-chain evidence.

rules.operator_decision: What fraction of jobs to run in cheaper deferred batch mode vs on-demand, trading 50% cost for a 72-hour completion horizon.

rules.operator_decision: Whether and how to escalate a failed attempt through model tiers (Flash -> Sonnet -> Opus -> Human), designed to keep human escalation under 1% because each escalation multiplies cost.

evidence_fields.source: experiment_spec.py:365-366 - DECLARED; workflow_runner.py:528-529 writes None only

rules.existing_backend_source: escalation_from/escalation_to are declared (experiment_spec.py:365-366) but runtime/workflow_runner.py:528-529 always writes None ('never retries a phase and never escalates a model mid-phase'). No automatic cascade exists; control/routing.py:110 is an offline recommendation and control/decisions.py:37 is proposal-only, never applied. scripts/cap_cascade_retrospective.py is retrospective-only. apps/website/data.js publishes verdicts.escalation E_x (~:6698). No Control Room endpoint and no recorded escalation cost.
rules.action: Intervene: escalate a failed attempt to the next tier (or human) and design the cascade bound to <1% human.
rules.cost_of_missing: Failures do not escalate automatically and escalation cost is never recorded, so the 28.2x price multiplier is a surprise; the operator cannot see or design the cascade as a policy arm.
rules.acceptance_walkthrough: 1. On a failed attempt, open R4a/R4c. 2. Confirm an escalation event is shown from -> to with its reason and cost, or an explicit 'no cascade armed' state. PASS: escalation tier, reason, and measured E_x cost are shown, or the absence is explicit; FAIL: escalation is a silent status change with no cost.

rules.operator_decision: What SLA buffer to set and whether to batch: never batch jobs whose SLA is under 2x observed queue depth; always keep an on-demand fallback.

evidence_fields.source: experiment_spec.py:373-374 - DECLARED, NO WRITER (worker.py:391,434 elapsed logged, never persisted)

rules.existing_backend_source: Queue COUNTS are EMITTED (control/pipeline_status.py:61-73; scripts/monitor.py; GET /api/matrix) and an aggregate SLA breach rate is computed (scripts/aggregate_workflow_metrics.py:706-748). queue_wait_ms/service_time_ms/due_at/deadline_slack are declared (experiment_spec.py:338-374) with ZERO writers; worker.py:391,434 computes elapsed but only logs it. The Control Room parity TIMING_FIELDS (apps/control_room/static/parity.js:458-471) marks queue_wait/service_time 'unknown'. No SLA buffer arithmetic exists anywhere.
rules.action: Intervene: add an on-demand fallback and hold batch work when queue depth threatens the SLA; set the 2x queue-depth rule.
rules.cost_of_missing: Queue wait and service time are invisible, so the 2x queue-depth rule cannot be applied; batch work silently breaches its SLA and the operator sees only a stuck queue.
rules.acceptance_walkthrough: 1. Open the queue lens (J8/J2). 2. Confirm queue depth and, per job, queue_wait/service_time or an explicit 'unknown'. 3. Confirm an SLA/fallback action when depth x 2 exceeds the horizon. PASS: queue wait and service time are measured (or explicitly unknown) and the 2x rule surfaces; FAIL: only raw counts are shown as if they were timings.

rules.action: Decide/audit: compare arms on outcomes per dollar and keep the value-maximizing policy; record the verdict.
